name: Czechoslovakia and Czechia
summary: Czechoslovakia was founded in 1918, occupied by Nazi Germany, ruled by communists (Prague Spring crushed in 1968), freed by the Velvet Revolution (1989) and split peacefully in 1993 into Czechia and Slovakia. This entry continues as Czechia.

knownFor.label: Prague Castle
knownFor.note: One of the largest castle complexes.

location.value: Central Europe, landlocked between Germany, Poland, Slovakia and Austria.

terrain.value: The Bohemian basin and uplands, with hills and mountains along the border.

climate.value: Temperate continental, with cold winters and warm summers.

resources.value: Coal, uranium (once important), timber, farmland and famous beer hops.

disasters.value: Severe floods in 1997 and 2002 hit Prague and Moravia.

population.value: 10,524,167 (2021 census); 10,915,839 (2025 estimate). The article read gives no 1990 total for Czechoslovakia.
population.source: Wikipedia: Czech Republic (checked 12 Nov 2026); Wikipedia: Czechoslovakia (checked 12 Nov 2026)

urbanisation.value: About 74% urban; Prague has about 1.3 million people, followed by Brno and Ostrava.

disease.value: Life expectancy around 79 years and good public health care.

migration.value: Most German speakers were forcibly expelled after 1945 (an organised transfer confirmed at Potsdam). Foreigners in 2021 numbered 658,564, led by Ukrainians and Slovaks (22% each), then Vietnamese (12%).
migration.source: Wikipedia: Czech Republic (checked 12 Nov 2026); Wikipedia: Czechoslovakia (checked 12 Nov 2026)

economicBase.value: Industry: Škoda Auto is the largest company by revenue (2018 figure).
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Czech Republic (checked 12 Nov 2026); Wikipedia: Czechoslovakia (checked 12 Nov 2026)

tradeRoutes.value: Central rail and road crossroads; EU single market since 2004.

wealth.value: One of the richest former communist countries.

moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Czech Republic (checked 12 Nov 2026); Wikipedia: Czechoslovakia (checked 12 Nov 2026)

inequality.value: Among the most equal countries in the EU.

governmentType.value: A parliamentary republic; the president has been elected directly since 2013.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Czech Republic (checked 12 Nov 2026); Wikipedia: Czechoslovakia (checked 12 Nov 2026)

keyRulers.value: Tomáš Masaryk (first president, 14 November 1918 to 14 December 1935). Václav Havel (president 1989–1992, per the infobox).
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Czech Republic (checked 12 Nov 2026); Wikipedia: Czechoslovakia (checked 12 Nov 2026)

succession.value: Governments change through elections; the president is chosen by direct vote.

institutions.value: Parliament, Constitutional Court and strong local government.

stability.value: The Munich Agreement (1938); the Prague Spring liberalisation was stopped by the Warsaw Pact invasion of 1968.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Czech Republic (checked 12 Nov 2026); Wikipedia: Czechoslovakia (checked 12 Nov 2026)

eliteConflict.value: Rivalry between Andrej Babiš’s ANO movement and centre-right parties.

armyAndTech.value: NATO member since 1999; a strong arms industry.

majorWars.value: German occupation of the Czech lands after the Munich Agreement (1938); the Warsaw Pact invasion of the night of 20–21 August 1968.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Czech Republic (checked 12 Nov 2026); Wikipedia: Czechoslovakia (checked 12 Nov 2026)

territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Czech Republic (checked 12 Nov 2026); Wikipedia: Czechoslovakia (checked 12 Nov 2026)

inventions.value: Otto Wichterle is credited with the modern contact lens (the article gives no date). Karel Čapek and the word “robot” are not mentioned.
inventions.source: Wikipedia: Czech Republic (checked 12 Nov 2026); Wikipedia: Czechoslovakia (checked 12 Nov 2026)

scienceEducation.value: Charles University, founded 1348, the first university in Central Europe.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Czech Republic (checked 12 Nov 2026); Wikipedia: Czechoslovakia (checked 12 Nov 2026)

openness.value: A very open, export-led economy, with strong car and engineering industries.

communicationTransport.value: Dense rail network; motorways; Prague metro.

religion.value: Czechs are described as tolerant and even indifferent towards religion; 56.9% had no religion (2021).
religion.source: Wikipedia: Czech Republic (checked 12 Nov 2026); Wikipedia: Czechoslovakia (checked 12 Nov 2026)

languageWriting.value: Czech (Slovak in Slovakia), very close to each other.

artsArchitecture.value: Prague’s Gothic and Baroque old town; composers Dvořák and Smetana; writers Kafka and Havel.

socialStructure.value: A large middle class, with a small Roma and Slovak minority.

sharedIdentity.value: Pride in the democratic First Republic (1918–38) and the Velvet Revolution.

dailyLife.value: Flats and family houses; dumplings, beer, weekend cottages (chata).

ideasReligions.value: Hussite reform, including the Bohemian Reformation and the Hussite Wars (1419–1434).
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Czech Republic (checked 12 Nov 2026); Wikipedia: Czechoslovakia (checked 12 Nov 2026)
